description: Composite five-panel figure mixing X-ray diffraction (XRD) line-profile analysis, moment plots and a dislocation-density trend. (a) is the (110) XRD peak profile, Normalised intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (°) from 43.5 to 45.0, with three curves — 98%CR (black, clearly broadened), 750°C, 5min (red) and 750°C, 60min (blue) — all peaking near 44.2°. The inset in (a) stacks the complete XRD profiles (Normalised intensity vs 2θ = 40–120°) for 98%CR, 750C_5min and 750C_60min, each with its calculated ("_calc") curve, indexing (110), (200), (211), (220) and (310) reflections of ferrite. (b)–(d) plot the second-order moment M₂ (solid) and fourth-order moment M₄/q² (dashed), in nm², against q (nm⁻¹) for 98%CR (b), 750°C, 5min (c) and 750°C, 60min (d); M₂ rises steeply to ~2.2×10⁶, ~4.4×10⁴ and ~3.5×10⁶ nm² respectively while M₄/q² stays much lower and near-linear. (e) is a semi-log plot of Dislocation density (m⁻², 1E11–1E16) vs Annealing time (min) with three points: ~2×10¹⁵ (98%CR, 0 min), ~6×10¹² (5 min) and ~1×10¹² (60 min). Together the panels show that the ferrite (110) broadening of the cold-rolled Fe-6.8Al sample arises from a very high dislocation density, which drops about three orders of magnitude on annealing at 750 °C.

subfigures.description: (110) XRD peak profile, Normalised intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (°) 43.5–45.0, three curves labelled 98%CR (black), 750°C, 5min (red) and 750°C, 60min (blue), all centred near 44.2°; the 98%CR curve is markedly broader and lower. Inset stacks full XRD profiles over 2θ = 40–120° with calculated fits and indices (110), (200), (211), (220), (310).
Plot of M₂ (solid) and M₄/q² (dashed), in nm², vs q (nm⁻¹) for the 98%CR sample; y-axis 0–3.0×10⁶ nm², x-axis 0–1.0×10⁻² nm⁻¹; M₂ rises to ~2.2×10⁶ nm² at the highest q.
Same moment plot for 750°C, 5min; y-axis 0–6.0×10⁴ nm², x-axis 0–1.6×10⁻¹ nm⁻¹; M₂ reaches ~4.4×10⁴ nm² with M₄/q² ~1.4×10⁴ nm².
Same moment plot for 750°C, 60 min; y-axis 0–4.0×10⁶ nm², x-axis 0–1.4×10⁻² nm⁻¹; M₂ reaches ~3.5×10⁶ nm² and M₄/q² ~1.1×10⁶ nm².

Semi-log plot of Dislocation density (m⁻²) on a 1E11–1E16 scale vs Annealing time (min), three square markers joined by a dashed line: ~2×10¹⁵ (cold rolled, 0 min), ~6×10¹² (5 min) and ~1×10¹² (60 min).

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows three (110) XRD peak profiles over 2θ = 43.5–45.0°, labelled 98%CR (black), 750°C, 5min (red) and 750°C, 60min (blue), all centred near 44.2°.
The 98%CR (110) peak is visibly broader and has a lower peak height than the two annealed profiles, which are narrower and similar to each other.

The inset in (a) stacks complete XRD profiles over 2θ = 40–120° for 98%CR, 750C_5min and 750C_60min, each with a calculated ('_calc') curve, with reflections indexed (110), (200), (211), (220) and (310).

Panels (b)–(d) plot M₂ (solid line) and M₄/q² (dashed line), both in nm², against q (nm⁻¹), with the sample condition printed in the top-left of each panel: 98%CR, 750°C, 5min and 750°C, 60 min respectively.

Panel (e) uses a logarithmic dislocation-density axis (1E11 to 1E16 m⁻²) and shows only three data points joined by a dashed line, falling from ~2×10¹⁵ m⁻² at the cold-rolled condition to ~6×10¹² m⁻² at 5 min and ~1×10¹² m⁻² at 60 min.

The caption states panel (a) is the (110) peak profile, that the inset shows the complete XRD profiles, and that (b), (c) and (d) are the M and M₄/q² versus q plots for the Fe-6.8Al samples after 98%CR and isothermal annealing at 750 °C for 5 min and 60 min.
The caption describes (e) as the variation of dislocation density for Fe-6.8Al low-density steel in different conditions.
The citing text states the full XRD scan in the inset of Fig. 7a confirms the formation of the ferrite phase in the Fe-6.8Al samples in the three conditions.

The citing text states Rietveld refinement was performed on the inset XRD profiles using MAUD software, with results presented in Table 3, and that the lattice micro-strain decreases after annealing from the cold-rolled state.

The citing text attributes the large (110) peak broadening of the 98%CR sample to lattice micro-strain imparted during cold rolling, i.e. to dislocations as a lattice imperfection (crystallite size and lattice strain being the two primary imperfections).
The citing text states that dislocation-induced broadening becomes significant when dislocation density exceeds 5×10¹² m⁻².

The citing text states the dislocation density falls by about three orders of magnitude upon annealing until 60 min at 750 °C relative to the cold-rolled sample, attributed to recrystallisation of ferrite at 5 min and subsequent grain growth at 60 min.

The y-axis scales of the moment panels differ by orders of magnitude (0–3.0×10⁶, 0–6.0×10⁴ and 0–4.0×10⁶ nm² for b, c, d), while the corresponding x-axis ranges also differ (to 1.0×10⁻², 1.6×10⁻¹ and 1.4×10⁻² nm⁻¹).
